title: Affine-space intersection dimension lower bound
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $n\in\mathbf N$. Let $A,B\subseteq|\mathbf A^n_k|$ be nonempty closed subsets of affine space [def-sbc-affine-space], with their induced topologies. Suppose $\dim A=a$ and $\dim B=b$ for integers $a,b\geq0$, where dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Suppose $A$ and $B$ are equidimensional, meaning that every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $A$ has dimension $a$ and every irreducible component of $B$ has dimension $b$. Then every irreducible component of $A\cap B$ has dimension at least $a+b-n$. In particular, if $A\cap B$ is nonempty, then $\dim(A\cap B)\geq a+b-n$. No nonemptiness conclusion for $A\cap B$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0B2Q, varieties-lemma-intersection-in-affine-space, lines 6338-6362; last sentence is its immediate nonempty-intersection consequence.

proof.text: Put $R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. The description of closed sets in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] gives ideals $I,J\subset R$ with $A=V(I)$ and $B=V(J)$. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion] and [def-weil-closed-immersion], these are closed subschemes of $\operatorname{Spec}R=\mathbf A^n_k$, with images $V(I),V(J)$. Explicitly, the primes of $R/I$ correspond to primes of $R$ containing $I$, by inverse image and $\mathfrak p\mapsto\mathfrak p/I$; the basic open of $\bar f$ corresponds to $V(I)\cap D(f)$. Thus the induced topologies are exactly those in the item. Consequently $X,Y$ are nonempty, finite type over $k$, and equidimensional of dimensions $a,b$.

source.place: Tag 0B2Q, first sentence of proof: choose closed subscheme structures on the two closed subsets.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $T=X\times_kY=\operatorname{Spec}S$ where $S=(R/I)\otimes_k(R/J)$. Write $u_i=\bar x_i\otimes1$ and $v_i=1\otimes\bar x_i$. The $2n$ elements $u_i,v_i$ generate $S$ over $k$; its presentation is $k[u_1,\ldots,u_n,v_1,\ldots,v_n]/(I(u),J(v))$, since maps out of either algebra are precisely pairs of $k$-algebra maps from $R/I,R/J$. Let $H=(u_1-v_1,\ldots,u_n-v_n)$ and $D=S/H$. There is an explicit isomorphism $D\cong R/(I+J)$: both $u_i,v_i$ map to the class of $x_i$; inversely the class of $x_i$ maps to the common class of $u_i,v_i$. These maps respect all relations and their composites fix the generators. Hence $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$ is a closed subscheme of $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion], and its underlying space is homeomorphic to $A\cap B=V(I+J)$ by the prime/basic-open correspondence of step 1. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], $S$ is Noetherian. Both $T,Z$ are finite type over $k$ by their displayed finite generating sets.

source.place: Tag 0B2Q, diagonal equations in the first paragraph of the proof; explicit coordinate-ring presentation.

proof.text: The structure map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat: every affine coordinate algebra is a $k$-vector space, so [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] apply. Thus the projection $p:T\to Y$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. The finite-type base-change and composition assertions of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] show that $p$ and $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are finite type. In particular $p$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are locally finite type, as required for the fibre-dimension equality.

source.place: Tag 0B2M, lemma-dimension-product-locally-algebraic, proof of (1), flatness of the projection.

proof.text: Fix $z\in T$ with projections $x\in X,y\in Y$. Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ base changed along $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $\dim_z(T_y)=\dim_xX$, since the fibre of $X$ over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $X$. Apply [lem-sbc-flat-composite-fibre-dimension-at-point] to $T\xrightarrow pY\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, using step 3. The fibres over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are $T,Y$ themselves, so $\dim_zT=\dim_z(T_y)+\dim_yY=\dim_xX+\dim_yY$. Finally [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension], with the whole schemes as the opens and the equidimensionality in step 1, gives $\dim_xX=a$ and $\dim_yY=b$. Thus $\dim_zT=a+b$ for every $z\in T$. These are local topological dimensions, not local-ring dimensions.

source.place: Tags 0B2Q and 0B2M(1); the pointwise product-dimension formula, derived from Morphisms Tags 02FY and 02JS.

proof.text: Let $C$ be any irreducible component of $Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], $C=V_D(\mathfrak q)$ for a minimal prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$. Let $P\subset S$ be its inverse image. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], the point $\eta=P$ of $T$ has closure $V_S(P)$, which is exactly the image of $C$ under the closed immersion $Z\to T$. Thus $C$, regarded as a closed subset of $T$, is nonempty and irreducible, and $\eta$ is its generic point. Since $S$ is Noetherian and $H\subset P$, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] applied to the $n$ differences gives $\operatorname{ht}_S(P)\leq\operatorname{ht}_{D}(\mathfrak q)+n=n$. Indeed the only prime contained in the minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ is itself, so every chain ending below it has length zero. Repeated or zero differences cause no problem: the bound is by the length $n$ of the generating list.

source.place: Tag 0B2Q, local quotient dimension estimate using Algebra Tag 00KW; generic-point version of the same height estimate.

proof.text: For the whole affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}S$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $\mathcal O_{T,\eta}$ with $S_P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], $\dim S_P=\operatorname{ht}_S(P)\leq n$. Apply [lem-kun-dimension-formula] to the finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ at $\eta$ and use step 4: $a+b=\dim\mathcal O_{T,\eta}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_T(\eta)$. Apply [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] to the closed irreducible subset $C\subset T$ with generic point $\eta$: $\dim C=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_T(\eta)$. The two equations give $a+b=\dim S_P+\dim C\leq n+\dim C$, hence $\dim C\geq a+b-n$. All terms being subtracted are finite integers: $\dim S_P\leq n$, and the displayed equality has finite left side $a+b$. The homeomorphism in step 2 carries this bound to every component of $A\cap B$.

source.place: Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic, (6),(10), equivalently Morphisms Tag 02FX; final dimension conversion in Tag 0B2Q.

proof.text: For completeness, suppose $A\cap B$ is nonempty. Its dimension is a finite nonnegative integer $d\leq a$: any closed irreducible chain in $A\cap B$ is such a chain in $A$, since the intersection is closed in $A$. By [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], a chain of length $d$ is attained. Its last member $C$ is an irreducible component: a strictly larger irreducible subset would have irreducible closure strictly containing $C$, extending that chain to length $d+1$. The same chain and monotonicity give $\dim C=d$. Step 6 therefore gives $\dim(A\cap B)=d\geq a+b-n$. If the intersection is empty, it has no irreducible components, so the first conclusion is vacuous and the second is conditional. No nonemptiness of an affine intersection was used.

source.place: Tag 0B2Q, immediate nonempty-intersection consequence of the componentwise estimate.

The item has no new nodes or repair note. Its statement matches Stacks 0B2Q (varieties.tex 6338-6362) and is unchanged. Proof checked step by step. Step 1: closed sets are V(I), and Spec(R/I) maps homeomorphically onto V(I) by the quotient closed immersion. Step 2: T=Spec((R/I)⊗(R/J)), the diagonal quotient D≅R/(I+J) (checked on generators both ways), and S is Noetherian because it is a finitely generated k-algebra. Step 3: X→Spec k is flat (affine criterion plus field-module flatness), so p is flat by base change, and finite type follows from both clauses of the composition/base-change node. Step 4: dim_z T=a+b by 02FY and 02JS, exactly as in the proof of 0B2M(1); def-kun-dimension and def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point give the same local dimension. Step 5: a component is V(q) with q a minimal prime, and the n-generator bound gives ht P≤ht q+n=n with S Noetherian and H⊆P. Step 6: O_{T,η}=S_P, so dim S_P=ht P; then the dimension formula 02FX and dim C=trdeg κ_T(η) give dim C≥a+b-n. Step 7 is genuinely elementary: a chain of maximal length has an irreducible component as its top member. Edge cases checked: n=0, disjoint subsets, a+b<n, reducible equidimensional sets, nonreduced quotients, non-closed fields. No duplicate node (rg -L for 0B2Q, 0B2M and 00KW; lem-sfb-scheme-product-dimension states only total dimension). The dependency closure contains no cycle. No SGA citation. The only citer, the parent projective-intersection lemma, first reduces to irreducible subsets, so its use of the equidimensionality hypothesis is sound. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem AffineSpace.closed_intersection_dimension (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (A B : Set (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) (Spec (.of k)))) (hAClosed : IsClosed A) (hBClosed : IsClosed B) (hANonempty : A.Nonempty) (hBNonempty : B.Nonempty) (a b : ℕ) (hADim : topologicalKrullDim A = (a : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hBDim : topologicalKrullDim B = (b : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hAEquidim : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents ↥A, topologicalKrullDim C = (a : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hBEquidim : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents ↥B, topologicalKrullDim C = (b : WithBot ℕ∞)) : (∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents ↥(A ∩ B), ((a + b : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim C + (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ ((A ∩ B).Nonempty → ((a + b : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim ↥(A ∩ B) + (n : WithBot ℕ∞))
